children: Alumis said its trial of a lupus treatment didn't meet its primary or secondary endpoints.

The Phase 2b trial of envudeucitinib as a treatment for moderate-to-severe systemic lupus erythematosus didn't meet the goal of improvements in overall disease activity based on various indicator assessments.

Patients with high interferon gene signature, which typically signals lupus, normally respond to interferon pathway-targeted therapies such as envudeucitinib and show lower placebo response rates. However, those patients were unexpectedly under-represented in the trial, reducing response rates in the overall population, Alumis said.

Patients in that subgroup did show "robust clinical responses" to the treatment, which Alumis said was promising enough to keep moving forward with trials. Management plans to engage regulators to discuss developing a Phase 3 trial of envudeucitinib.
The drug was also well tolerated with no new safety signals observed.
Alumis remains on track to submit a new drug application for envudeucitinib in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in the fourth quarter of this year.
